narrative:
The FY2026 net interest income baseline is PLN 3.33B across five business segments, up 12.5% on the FY2025 actual of PLN 2.96B. The step-up is almost entirely structural: the Citi Handlowy retail book, live on VeloBank systems since 15 June 2026, adds PLN 22.1B of deposits and PLN 6B of loans to the combined balance sheet.

Retail remains the engine at PLN 2.23B (67% of NII), led by current accounts and consumer lending. Affluent & Private Banking almost doubles to PLN 375M as ex-Citi relationship clients move onto VeloBank pricing.

Key risk: the baseline already absorbs the first NBP cuts, but the ALCO ambition of PLN 3.40B requires deposit repricing and spread discipline in later phases to close a PLN 70M gap.

signals.title: Citi Handlowy Retail Integration Completed
signals.excerpt: Migration of the Citi Handlowy retail business completed on 15 June 2026: PLN 22.1B of deposits, PLN 6B of loans, PLN 8.9B AuM and ~1,600 employees now on VeloBank systems.

signals.title: Management Commentary — Rate Headwind
signals.excerpt: Management flagged NBP rate cuts as the key earnings headwind for net interest income, with deposit pricing discipline and balance-sheet growth as offsets.

signals.title: Target Organisation — Restructuring Programme
signals.excerpt: VeloBank announced a target-organisation programme affecting up to 950 roles to align the combined bank's cost base after the Citi integration.
